title: Perfect completeness for quadratic character pairs
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\ell:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ and $q:\mathbb{F}_2^{n\times n}\to\mathbb{F}_2$, and suppose there is $\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ such that $\ell(x)=\sum_i\gamma_i x_i$ for every $x$ and $q(B)=\sum_{i,j}\gamma_i\gamma_jB_{ij}$ for every matrix $B$. Then the quadratic character pair tester accepts the oracle formed from $\ell$ and $q$ with probability exactly $1$. All sums and products are in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
hypotheses_covered: $\ell$ maps binary vectors of length $n$ to $\mathbb{F}_2$
There is $\gamma\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$ representing $\ell$ by the binary dot product and $q$ by the associated matrix pairing
